transcript.text: Indesit washer dryer washes fine but the drying cycle doesn't get warm at all, clothes come out cold and wet after 2 hours. Model is XWDE 96 something.

It sounds like the heating element isn't working, but on washer-dryers, 'no heat' or 'cold clothes' is often caused by restricted airflow rather than a broken part. Please check if the lint filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) is clean, and if your model has a separate condenser unit, ensure that is clear of fluff. Also, did you dry a load size appropriate for drying (typically about half the wash capacity)? Once you've checked those, let me know what you found.
Load was about 4kg. I've not checked the lint filter yet, will do that now. Should I be looking at anything else while I'm at it? The door glass was stone cold during the dry too.

[Heading: Blocked airflow or failed heating element]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. A stone-cold door glass strongly suggests the heating element isn't activating at all, rather than just being restricted by fluff. However, we must rule out airflow issues first because a blocked filter can trip safety cut-outs that stop the heater from working. Please check the lint filter and condenser (if fitted) for fluff buildup now. If it stays completely cold even with a clean filter, the heating element or its thermal cut-out is likely faulty.
Ok, I've unplugged it and will check the filter and condenser now. There's been no burning smell and nothing tripping, in case that matters. If it's all clear, what do I do next?

That's good to hear about no burning smell or tripping; it suggests we aren't dealing with an immediate electrical short. Since you're checking the filter now, please look for any fluff buildup in both the pump filter (bottom front) and the condenser unit if your model has one. Clean them thoroughly if needed, then plug the machine back in and run a short drying cycle to see if it gets warm.
Ok, filter and condenser are done. Should I plug it back in and run a dry now, or is there something else to check if it's still cold?

[Heading: Faulty drying heating element or thermal cut-out]
The 'stone-cold' door glass strongly points to an electrical fault in the drying heater or its safety thermal cut-out rather than just airflow. Please plug it back in and run a short drying cycle (about 30 minutes). After about 15 minutes, carefully feel the door glass or the drum rim. If it is still stone cold, the heating element or its thermal cut-out has likely failed and will need replacement by an engineer. If it gets warm but stays damp, we may have missed some fluff deeper in the condenser ducting.

Ok, will plug it back in and run a short dry. Just so you know, the door glass was already stone cold on the last full dry, so I'd expect the same. If it's still cold, what would an engineer actually be replacing?

[Heading: Failed drying heating element or thermal cut-out]
If the door glass remains stone cold after you run that short dry cycle, an engineer would typically replace the drying heating element or the thermal cut-out (the safety fuse wired in series with it). On Indesit washer-dryers, these are often located behind the front panel or at the bottom of the drum. Because this involves opening the casing and working on live electrical components, it is not a safe job for a homeowner to attempt. Please run that short test now; if it stays cold, you will need to call an engineer to replace one of those parts.
